subject.title: fix(security): add default pidsLimit for sandbox containers

question: Should OpenClaw change the Docker sandbox default from no PID cap to a built-in 1024 PID cap, and what explicit opt-out or upgrade contract should existing users get?
rationale: The diff changes a sandbox security default for all unset configs, and automation should not choose the permanent cap value or whether existing Docker-default behavior remains available.

options.title: Default cap with explicit opt-out
options.body: Land this direction only after making the default, override, and unlimited or Docker-default opt-out contract valid in schema, docs, tests, and real Docker proof.

options.title: Strict cap without opt-out
options.body: Accept that some existing sandbox workloads may break and require maintainer-owned release notes plus upgrade guidance.

options.title: Keep current default
options.body: Close or replace the PR and document `pidsLimit` as an operator-managed hardening setting instead of a core default.

recommendation.title: Default cap with explicit opt-out
recommendation.body: Land this direction only after making the default, override, and unlimited or Docker-default opt-out contract valid in schema, docs, tests, and real Docker proof.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter Steinberger has recent sandbox security hardening history on the same Docker sandbox surfaces.
